cohort: 398 mothers whose fetus had a nuchal translucency higher than the 95th percentile between 2009 and 2018 at a level 3 maternity unit in France
finding: Fetuses with increased nuchal translucency had a higher risk of chromosomal abnormalities, morphological abnormalities, hypotrophy, and cesarean birth, while 17% of liveborn children with previously increased nuchal translucency had psychomotor disorders.
mod_finding: Fetuses with a nuchal translucency ≥ 3.5 mm were at higher risk of birth by cesarean (p=0.04).
